source.title: Just Align $\bm{x}$: Aligning Predictions, Not Representations
source.authors: Yuyao Zhang; Yuwei Hu; Ziyang Mai; Yu-Wing Tai

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses representation-alignment methods and reports how they affect feature decodability in JiT and SiT, but it does not test whether independently trained models become more similar in their representations as scale or capability increases.
record.gate_note: The study does not measure similarity between independently trained models, cross-modal alignment, shared features, or representation interchangeability. Its REPA probe results concern linear accessibility of specified targets, not representational convergence as defined by the claim versions. FID results for alignment methods are not rows because they report generation quality, not convergence.
record.test_reason: The paper is a diffusion-training method paper (JAx). Its probe results measure how REPA, an auxiliary loss deliberately aligning hidden features to DINOv2, changes linear decodability of DINO features and residuals. This is induced alignment by training objective, not convergence arising between independently trained models, so no version is tested. It neither relies on the convergence claim as a tool nor discusses it beyond citing representation-alignment methods.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors argue that hidden-feature alignment (REPA) in pixel-space JiT can trade access to complementary image variation for semantic-feature access. They propose JAx, which aligns clean-image predictions across Markov-coupled noise levels. JAx improves FID across JiT-B/L/H with lower gradient variance and is compatible with PixelREPA.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes hidden-feature alignment and introduces prediction-space supervision; it does not reproduce a measurement of representational convergence.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported residual-feature probe changes differ by model family and layer: JiT has decreases that largely diminish toward the output, whereas SiT has increases at all measured layers.

fits_no_version.finding: At epoch 200, REPA raises linear decodability of DINO features at the alignment layer (+0.182 JiT, +0.215 SiT). It lowers decodability of the DINO-complementary residual in JiT (−0.052) but raises it in SiT (+0.021). The JiT deficit largely vanishes by the penultimate layer.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Explicit feature-alignment objectives in pixel-space diffusion models raise accessibility of the aligned features. The effect on complementary image variation depends on the model family and the layer.

record.problems: The probe findings are limited to evaluated settings at epoch 200; the text does not state uncertainty estimates for them. The study does not measure representational similarity or convergence between independently trained models.
record.rows_left_out: FID results comparing REPA, SRA, Self-Flow, JAx, and other methods are omitted because they report generation quality rather than representational convergence. Other probe values that are shown only in Figure 2 are not extracted when the text does not state them.

untested.parts: All; no similarity between independently trained models across scale is measured.
All; linear probes to DINO targets are measured only after training with an alignment loss, not as cross-model mapping of independently trained models.

record.verdict_notes: Relation changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only': the paper cites REPA-style alignment methods but does not discuss representational convergence as a phenomenon. The rows are fine as extracted but bear on no version; the alignment is induced by the training loss.
